lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: What if, for twenty-four hours, one AI ran an entire city? No mayor. No traffic cops. Just the AI... and a clock.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Six A.M. Every traffic light in the city syncs at once. Buses only stop where people are actually waiting. Rush hour... just disappears.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Noon. Drones drop deliveries in minutes. The power grid shifts energy before anyone turns on the AC. Hospitals get ready before the ambulance even calls.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Four P.M. One sensor misreads a flooded street. The AI reroutes ten thousand cars... onto one bridge.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Traffic locks up. Deliveries stall. The grid panics and cuts power to protect itself. One tiny mistake... and the whole city freezes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Midnight. The AI fixes it in seconds, faster than any human could. But nobody can explain why it happened.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And this isn't science fiction. Google's AI already helps time traffic lights in cities like Seattle and Rio. So the real question isn't whether AI can run a city... it's who's in charge when it gets it wrong.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Follow me, and comment CITY... and I'll send you the cities already testing this.
